# Cold-night shelter at St Aidan's hall: brief

The council has asked us to open the hall as a warm place on nights when the forecast is below freezing. It runs from the first cold night in December until the end of February. Nobody from the church office will be there overnight.

## What we know

- The hall has 30 camp beds in the store cupboard and 30 blankets. It also has 12 sleeping bags.
- Up to 6 volunteers can be on a night. We have 14 trained volunteers in total, and each has said they can do about 4 nights a month.
- The hall has one electric heater bank and a kitchen with a kettle, a hob and a microwave. The last electric bill for a winter evening event was £38.
- The council gives us £600 for the whole season. We have spent £90 so far on a first-aid kit and signs.
- The nearest A&E is 11 km away. The ambulance station is 6 km away. The hall has a landline and the volunteers have their own phones.
- The hall is next to a car park and a bus stop. The last bus on the route leaves at 23:10.
- The hall has two fire exits and one front door. The fire alarm panel is in the entrance lobby.
- Guests are adults who are sleeping outside. Some drink, and some have dogs. The hall's insurance covers dogs but only on the ground floor.
- Most of the volunteers have never done an overnight shift. Two are nurses and one is a retired police officer.
